text:
jason: Heads-up — ran a 1h stress with 500 concurrent infer requests and saw a cluster of GPU OOMs at ~30m in. P50 ok, but p99 latency and OOMs spike.
priya: Ugh. Any obvious culprit from profiler?
jason: nvprof shows big peaks in workspace alloc right before OOMs. Also our KV prefill rate doubles under certain batched workloads.
jin: Can you paste the short profiler dump?
jason: ```
# simplified nvprof allocation trace (tail)
ALLOC 0x7f3...  54MB  2026-03-12T10:30:12Z  kWorkspaceAlloc
ALLOC 0x7f3...  128MB 2026-03-12T10:30:12Z  kv_prefill_buf
FREE  0x7f3...  54MB  2026-03-12T10:30:12Z
OOM  -       0B   2026-03-12T10:30:13Z  cudaMalloc failed
```
jason: The pattern: lots of small frees interleaved with a large prefills that try to reserve contiguous memory, fragmentation prevents it, then workspace alloc fails.
alex: So fragmentation + aggressive prefill = bad. Any per-request caps right now?
jin: We have a per-request soft_cap for KV prefill at 64MB but it’s a recommendation, not enforced. Plus decode path may allocate additional transient buffers that push it over.
priya: We saw tail latency increases when sequence length distribution had heavy long-tail. Batching heuristics coalesced long and short seqs into larger batches, causing big workspace.
martha: What about buffer reuse? Are we occasionally allocating distinct buffers instead of reusing pooled ones?
jason: Yes — allocator hot-path sometimes returns non-reusable chunk for kv_prefill_buf because sizes don't match power-of-two bucket. Leads to fragmentation over longer runs.
theo: Ideas: 1) enforce per-request hard caps (prefill_max_bytes), 2) promote best-effort compaction / suballoc on eviction, 3) make decode allocate from same pool as prefill so reuse is possible, 4) kernel fallbacks that use smaller temp workspace.
priya: I can sketch config change for 1 and 3. For 2 — compaction on-device is expensive. Maybe try "soft-reserve": reserve a small contiguous slab per-GPU for prefill emergencies and throttle prefill if slab low.
jin: That sounds promising. Also add an eviction policy tied to age+size: evict small older kv segments first to reduce fragmentation.
alex: Could we change batching heuristic to avoid mixing very long sequences with short ones? Maybe a conservative split when seq_length variance in batch > threshold.
martha: Yes, adaptive batching can help reduce max workspace per batch. We can tune batcher to prefer bins by seq len quantiles.
priya: Here's a prototype config (will push to staging):
```json
{
  "kv": {
    "per_request_hard_cap_bytes": 83886080,  /* 80MB */
    "soft_reserve_slab_bytes": 268435456,   /* 256MB per-GPU */
    "eviction_policy": "age_then_small_first",
    "compaction_enabled": false
  },
  "batcher": {
    "max_seq_variance": 0.25,
    "prefer_sorted_by_length": true
  },
  "allocator": {
    "bucket_sizes": [16384, 65536, 262144, 1048576],
    "reuse_threshold": 0.8
  }
}
```
jin: Tests?
jason: Ran a 30m canary with the hard cap + soft_reserve simulation (no compaction) — OOMs dropped from 7 -> 0, p99 latency reduced by ~180ms. But throughput down ~4%.
priya: That's acceptable as a staged rollout: enable hard cap + batcher change in hosted API for low-tenancy customers, monitor.
theo: Need metrics: per-GPU free-slab, evictions/sec, fragmentation ratio (largest_free_chunk / total_free). Also add CI perf test to catch regressions.
devops-bot: [alert] perf/regressions job failed: p99 increased 120ms on model-5 in nightly. See: https://ci.internal/perf/2026-03-12/42
jin: That CI failure likely from earlier attempt with compaction enabled — compaction added lock contention. We shouldn't enable it in prod yet.
priya: Plan: 1) promote per-request hard cap (80MB) 2) add batcher split rule for high variance 3) soft reserve slab 256MB per-GPU 4) add observability (fragmentation ratio + slab usage) 5) run canaries + ramp.
martha: I'll add allocator introspection endpoint to export bucket occupancy heatmap.
jason: Also add a temporary runtime flag to force decode-from-pool to validate reuse gains.
priya: I'll run a focused profiling job: compare memory churn with decode-from-pool vs current.
jin: If canary numbers look good, let's ship to hosted with a gradual rollout and rollback flag.
priya: Will open a PR with config + metrics dashboard links.
jason: Thanks — good triage. Follow-ups: PR link, canary run id, and update on compaction experiments. :+1:
devops-bot: [note] scheduled canary: run_id=canary-2026-03-12-08, targets=hosted-us-west-2, ramp=10%
